about: GPU-host window job for narrate/bench/host_run.py (bench plan, docs/agent-notes/2026-10-22-narrate-bench-plan.md). Dollar-brace values come from the environment (run-bench.sh reads them from the private bench.env); this file holds no host path and no voice. The voice registry is a private, hash-bound file (voices_file) that never enters git. Weights use narrate-fetch's layout (<weights>/hf/<source id>/<file>) and their sha256 values from narrate/bench/sources.json. VK_DRIVER_FILES is set to vulkan_icd (RADV) for every engine. Window 2 (operator ruling J83(a); the bench plan's addendum of 2026-10-26) runs seed 1 only and one voice per window, in the arm order below; the two -cut arms are matched controls that clone from the same max14s cut and cut transcript as A3-gpu, so SIM compares like for like.

A2-gpu-alt.about: Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base through qwentts.cpp 5916bf7c, ICL cloning: --ref-wav plus the verified --ref-text. One model load; --stream-by-line makes every chunk one stdin line.

A1-gpu.about: Ming-3.0-tts-0.5B (bf16 GGUF) through audio.cpp 47c2756e, --task clon. Ming's prompt and output share a 512-position context of about 80 ms patches, so a 30 to 35 s reference with its transcript leaves almost no room for a 300-codepoint chunk; the smoke's duration check then falls back to speaker-embedding conditioning (voice_ref without reference_text), recorded as a deviation. Decoy 2: two chunks in the preset voice UK_George (template ip), no cloning.

A3-gpu.about: VoxCPM2 (bf16 GGUF) through audio.cpp 47c2756e. At this pin a request's voice_ref is VoxCPM2's reference audio, and its reference_text is the prompt transcript, used only with prompt audio (the request's audio). Variant ultimate sends the reference as both, the model card's ultimate clone; reference-only sends voice_ref alone, the controllable clone. Run 1's ref-text variant sent voice_ref plus reference_text, so its transcript would have gone unused; it crashed before that mattered. voxcpm2.mem_saver is already true by default at this pin.

reference.about: The AudioVAE encoder takes at most voxcpm2.audiovae_encoder_sample_capacity samples (default 240000) at the model's audio_vae_config.sample_rate (16000), after padding up to a multiple of patch_size x prod(encoder_rates) = 4 x 640 = 2560: references up to 238080 samples, 14.88 s. Run 1's 34.75 s reference exited 1 with 'VoxCPM2 AudioVAE encoder sample capacity exceeded'. The arm clones from the voice's cut max14s (narrate/bench/ref_cut.py; private voices file), at least 5 s per the VoxCPM2 usage guide's 5 to 30 s practical range. The reference and the prompt are the same clip, so both encodes fit.

A2-gpu-alt-cut.about: Matched-cut control of A2-gpu-alt (J83(a) addendum, 2026-10-26): the same runtime, inputs, settings and variant; the reference is the voice's max14s cut and its cut transcript (--ref-wav, --ref-text), the clip A3-gpu clones from, instead of the full clip. Scored against the full clip like every arm.

reference.about: A3-gpu's cut and its length bounds; qwentts.cpp has no encoder limit of its own here.

A1-gpu-cut.about: Matched-cut control of A1-gpu (J83(a) addendum, 2026-10-26): the same runtime, inputs, settings and variants (ref-text first, speaker-embedding as the smoke fallback); the reference is the voice's max14s cut and its cut transcript, the clip A3-gpu clones from. About 12 s of prompt leaves Ming's 512-position context room for a chunk, so ref-text may pass the smoke here where it failed on the full clip in run 1; the receipt's variant says which conditioning ran. No decoy: decoy 2 renders once per window, inside A1-gpu.

reference.about: A3-gpu's cut and its length bounds; Ming's limit is its 512-position context, which the smoke checks.
